- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 20–40% after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 period windows; if forecast is >2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2σ; if below, increase by 1–2σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2 week “recovery” phases; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 5+ days, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for hidden support or policy-driven rebounds.
